title: Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science Module 1 – Earth’s Resources
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science Module 1. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
course: NSW Earth and Environmental Science Stage 6
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What is Earth’s thin, outermost compositional layer called?
What thick compositional layer lies beneath the crust?
Which compositional layer is mainly made of iron and nickel?
What process separated materials in the early Earth according to density?
Which early Earth sphere formed as water vapour cooled and condensed?
What scale ranks minerals from 1 to 10 by hardness?
What mineral property describes how light reflects from its surface?
What mineral test records the colour of its powdered form?
What mineral property describes breaking along smooth, flat planes?
What common mineral is made of silicon and oxygen with the formula SiO₂?
What rock type forms when magma or lava cools and solidifies?
What rock type commonly forms from compacted and cemented sediments?
What rock type forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
What process breaks exposed rock into smaller pieces without moving it?
What process turns loose sediments into sedimentary rock by compaction and cementation?
What dark organic material in soil forms from decomposed organisms?
Which soil particle is largest: sand, silt or clay?
Which soil particle is smallest: sand, silt or clay?
What name is given to a vertical section showing the layers of soil?
What term describes the ability of water to pass through soil or rock?
What type of dating places rocks or events in order without giving a numerical age?
What principle states that, in an undisturbed sequence, older sedimentary layers lie below younger ones?
questions.answer: The principle of superposition. Accept: superposition.

questions.prompt: What method uses radioactive decay to determine a numerical age for rocks or minerals?
What term describes a rock containing enough valuable mineral to be mined economically?
What exploration method sends energy waves into the ground and analyses their reflections?
questions.answer: A seismic survey. Accept: seismic surveying.

finalRound.prompt: What term describes the measured numerical age of a rock or geological event, usually given in years?
